title: Die vier kunstreichen Brüder
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 129. Text from Wikisource (twice proofread against the original). 1857 spelling preserved exactly.
about: KHM 129 follows four brothers who each take up a different trade — thieving, stargazing, hunting and tailoring — and prove their skill in one string of party tricks worked on a bird's nest before putting it to real use: spotting a captive princess on a rock in the open sea, stealing her from under a sleeping dragon, shooting the dragon dead in mid-air, and sewing a wrecked ship whole again on the water. Where such tales usually end with one brother marrying the princess, this one ends in a fair division instead — none of them gets her, and each gets half a kingdom. A cheerful heist story built entirely out of specialized skill.

sentences.t: Es war ein armer Mann, der hatte vier Söhne, wie die heran gewachsen waren, sprach er zu ihnen „liebe Kinder, ihr müßt jetzt hinaus in die Welt, ich habe nichts, das ich euch geben könnte;
sentences.l: There was a poor man, he had four sons; when they had grown up, he spoke to them “dear children, you must now out into the world, I have nothing that I could give you;
sentences.i: There was once a poor man who had four sons, and when they had grown up he said to them, “dear children, you must go out into the world now; I have nothing I could give you;
sentences.n: der hatte vier Söhne — the tale joins its clauses with a demonstrative der, “that one had”, where English wants a relative “who had”; the loose, spoken join is characteristic of the telling. ihr müßt jetzt hinaus in die Welt has no verb of motion at all: müssen carries the “must” and the direction word hinaus does the rest. The speech runs on into the next unit, so the closing quotation mark comes only there.

sentences.t: macht euch auf und geht in die Fremde, lernt ein Handwerk und seht wie ihr euch durchschlagt.“
sentences.l: set yourselves out and go into the foreign parts, learn a trade and see how you strike your way through.”
sentences.i: set out and go abroad, learn a trade and see how you make your own way.”
sentences.n: sich aufmachen — to set out, literally “to make oneself up”. die Fremde is the noun of fremd, foreign: the parts away from home. sich durchschlagen is to beat one’s way through, to get by; the reflexive euch belongs to it.

sentences.t: Da ergriffen die vier Brüder den Wanderstab, nahmen Abschied von ihrem Vater und zogen zusammen zum Thor hinaus.
sentences.l: Then the four brothers seized the wandering-staff, took leave of their father and drew out together through the gate.
sentences.i: So the four brothers took up the wanderer’s staff, said farewell to their father and went out together through the town gate.
sentences.n: den Wanderstab ergreifen is the set phrase for taking to the road. zum Thor hinaus — “out through the gate”: zu with hinaus frames the going-out. Thor is the 1857 spelling of Tor, the town gate.

sentences.t: Als sie eine Zeit lang gewandert waren, kamen sie an einen Kreuzweg, der nach vier verschiedenen Gegenden führte.
sentences.l: When they had wandered a time long, they came to a cross-way that led toward four different regions.
sentences.i: When they had travelled for a while, they came to a crossroads that led off into four different quarters.
sentences.n: eine Zeit lang — “for a time”; lang follows the stretch of time it measures. wandern is not idle rambling but travelling on foot, the ordinary way of getting anywhere in the tales.

sentences.t: Da sprach der älteste „hier müssen wir uns trennen, aber heut über vier Jahre wollen wir an dieser Stelle wieder zusammen treffen und in der Zeit unser Glück versuchen.“
sentences.l: Then the eldest spoke “here we must part ourselves, but today over four years we will meet together again at this place and in the meantime try our fortune.”
sentences.i: Then the eldest said, “here we must part, but four years from today we will meet again at this spot, and in between try our fortune.”
sentences.n: heut über vier Jahre — “four years from today”; über with a stretch of time reckons forward from now. sich trennen is reflexive where English simply parts. sprach, the past of sprechen, is the tales’ standard word for “said”.

sentences.t: Nun gieng jeder seinen Weg, und dem ältesten begegnete ein Mann, der fragte ihn wo er hinaus wollte und was er vor hätte.
sentences.l: Now each went his way, and to the eldest there met a man, who asked him where he wanted out to and what he had in mind.
sentences.i: Now each went his own way, and the eldest was met by a man who asked him where he was bound and what he intended.
sentences.n: begegnen takes the dative: dem ältesten begegnete ein Mann is “a man met the eldest”, with the person met in the dative. wo er hinaus wollte again has no verb of motion. was er vor hätte is vorhaben, to have in mind, with the particle vor split off.

sentences.t: „Ich will ein Handwerk lernen,“ antwortete er.
sentences.l: “I want to learn a trade,” he answered.
sentences.n: das Handwerk is a trade in the old sense — a craft learned by apprenticeship, with a guild behind it. The four brothers’ trades are the whole substance of this tale.

sentences.t: Da sprach der Mann „geh mit mir, und werde ein Dieb.“
sentences.l: Then the man said “go with me, and become a thief.”
sentences.i: Then the man said, “come along with me and become a thief.”
sentences.n: geh mit mir — German says “go with me” where English says “come with me”; direction is reckoned from where the speaker stands. werde is the imperative of werden, to become.

sentences.t: „Nein,“ antwortete er, „das gilt für kein ehrliches Handwerk mehr, und das Ende vom Lied ist, daß einer als Schwengel in der Feldglocke gebraucht wird.“
sentences.l: “No,” he answered, “that passes for no honest trade any more, and the end of the song is that one gets used as the clapper in the field-bell.”
sentences.i: “No,” he answered, “that no longer counts as an honest trade, and the end of the song is that a man is used as the clapper of the bell out in the field.”
sentences.n: für etwas gelten — to pass for, to count as. das Ende vom Lied, “the end of the song”, is how a thing finishes. The picture behind Schwengel in der Feldglocke is a hanged man swinging from the gallows like the clapper inside a bell; the gallows stood out in the open field. The exact turn of the joke is not certain, but the man’s answer about the Galgen in the next line shows plainly what is meant.

sentences.t: „O,“ sprach der Mann, „vor dem Galgen brauchst du dich nicht zu fürchten: ich will dich bloß lehren wie du holst was sonst kein Mensch kriegen kann, und wo dir niemand auf die Spur kommt.“
sentences.l: “Oh,” said the man, “of the gallows you need not be afraid: I will only teach you how you fetch what no other person can get, and where no one comes upon your trace.”
sentences.i: “Oh,” said the man, “you need not be afraid of the gallows: I will only teach you how to take what nobody else can get, and in such a way that no one comes on your track.”
sentences.n: sich fürchten vor — to be afraid of, with the reflexive dich. brauchen … nicht zu is the everyday “need not”. jemandem auf die Spur kommen — to get on someone’s track, with the person in the dative, dir.

sentences.t: Da ließ er sich überreden, ward bei dem Manne ein gelernter Dieb und ward so geschickt, daß vor ihm nichts sicher war, was er einmal haben wollte.
sentences.l: Then he let himself be talked over, became with the man a trained thief and became so deft that nothing was safe from him that he once wanted to have.
sentences.i: So he let himself be persuaded, became a trained thief under that man, and grew so deft that nothing he had a mind to was safe from him.
sentences.n: sich überreden lassen — “to let oneself be persuaded”; lassen with an infinitive is the regular German turn where English uses a passive. ward is the older past of werden, modern wurde. ein gelernter Dieb keeps the language of the guilds: gelernt means apprenticed and time-served, not “erudite”.

sentences.t: Der zweite Bruder begegnete einem Mann, der dieselbe Frage an ihn that, was er in der Welt lernen wollte.
sentences.l: The second brother met a man, who put the same question to him, what he wanted to learn in the world.
sentences.i: The second brother met a man who put the same question to him: what he meant to learn in the world.
sentences.n: eine Frage an jemanden thun — to put a question to someone. that is the 1857 spelling of tat, from thun, modern tun.

sentences.t: „Ich weiß es noch nicht“ antwortete er.
sentences.l: “I do not know it yet,” he answered.
sentences.i: “I do not know yet,” he answered.
sentences.n: German keeps the object es where English drops it — weiß es, “know it”.

sentences.t: „So geh mit mir und werde ein Sterngucker: nichts besser als das, es bleibt einem nichts verborgen.“
sentences.l: “Then go with me and become a star-gazer: nothing better than that, nothing stays hidden from one.”
sentences.i: “Then come with me and become a star-gazer: there is nothing better, nothing stays hidden from you.”
sentences.n: der Sterngucker is literally a “star-peeper” — a star-gazer, an astronomer. nichts besser als das leaves the verb out, as speech does. einem is the dative of man, “one”: nothing stays hidden from a person who has the craft.

sentences.t: Er ließ sich das gefallen und ward ein so geschickter Sterngucker, daß sein Meister, als er ausgelernt hatte und weiter ziehen wollte, ihm ein Fernrohr gab
sentences.l: He let that please him and became so deft a star-gazer that his master, when he had learned out and wanted to move on further, gave him a far-tube
sentences.i: He was content with that and became so skilled a star-gazer that his master, when he had served out his time and wished to move on, gave him a spyglass
sentences.n: sich etwas gefallen lassen — to put up with a thing, to be content with it. auslernen is to finish an apprenticeship. das Fernrohr is literally a “far-tube”, a telescope. The sentence runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: und zu ihm sprach „damit kannst du sehen was auf Erden und am Himmel vorgeht, und kann dir nichts verborgen bleiben.“
sentences.l: and said to him “with it you can see what goes on on earth and in the sky, and nothing can stay hidden from you.”
sentences.i: and said to him, “with this you can see what passes on earth and in the heavens, and nothing can remain hidden from you.”
sentences.n: vorgehen — to go on, to be happening (separable: geht vor). auf Erden keeps an old dative form in a fixed phrase, “on earth”. The second clause begins with its verb, kann, because the subject nichts follows it — a shorthand German allows where English must repeat “and nothing can”.

sentences.t: Den dritten Bruder nahm ein Jäger in die Lehre und gab ihm in allem, was zur Jägerei gehört, so guten Unterricht, daß er ein ausgelernter Jäger ward.
sentences.l: The third brother a huntsman took into apprenticeship and gave him in everything that belongs to hunting such good instruction that he became a fully trained huntsman.
sentences.i: A huntsman took the third brother as his apprentice and gave him such good teaching in everything belonging to the huntsman’s craft that he came out a trained huntsman.
sentences.n: Den dritten Bruder stands first although it is the object — the accusative den marks it, so German can put it in front for emphasis and English has to reorder. in die Lehre nehmen is to take on as an apprentice; die Lehre here is the apprenticeship, not a “lesson”.

sentences.t: Der Meister schenkte ihm beim Abschied eine Büchse und sprach „die fehlt nicht, was du damit aufs Korn nimmst, das triffst du sicher.“
sentences.l: The master gave him at parting a gun and said “that one does not miss; what you take onto the bead with it, that you hit for certain.”
sentences.i: At parting the master made him a present of a gun and said, “this one never misses: whatever you take aim at with it, that you will surely hit.”
sentences.n: aufs Korn nehmen — to take aim at. Das Korn is the little bead or foresight on the gun barrel that the marksman brings onto his target; the phrase is still current, and has nothing to do with corn here. fehlen in this line is “to miss”, not “to be lacking”.

sentences.t: Der jüngste Bruder begegnete gleichfalls einem Manne, der ihn anredete und nach seinem Vorhaben fragte.
sentences.l: The youngest brother met likewise a man, who addressed him and asked after his intention.
sentences.i: The youngest brother likewise met a man, who spoke to him and asked what he had in mind.
sentences.n: anreden — to address, to speak to (separable: redete an). Manne carries the old dative -e, which 1857 still prints.

sentences.t: „Hast du nicht Lust ein Schneider zu werden?“
sentences.l: “Have you no desire to become a tailor?”
sentences.i: “Would you not like to become a tailor?”
sentences.n: Lust haben zu — to have a mind to, to feel like; the German asks after the lad’s inclination rather than his will.

sentences.t: „Daß ich nicht wüßte,“ sprach der Junge, „das Krummsitzen von Morgens bis Abends, das Hin und Herfegen mit der Nadel und das Bügeleisen will mir nicht in den Sinn.“
sentences.l: “That I would not know,” said the lad, “the crooked-sitting from morning till evening, the sweeping to and fro with the needle and the pressing-iron will not into my mind.”
sentences.i: “Not that I know of,” said the lad; “the sitting hunched from morning to night, the flicking of the needle to and fro and the pressing-iron are not to my liking.”
sentences.n: Daß ich nicht wüßte is a set reply — “not that I know of”, with the subjunctive wüßte. das Krummsitzen and das Hin und Herfegen are turned into nouns by the article, which German does freely: the sitting-crooked, the sweeping-to-and-fro. mir nicht in den Sinn wollen — “will not go into my mind”, that is, does not appeal to me; the verb of motion is again left out after wollen.

sentences.t: „Ei was,“ antwortete der Mann, „du sprichst wie dus verstehst: bei mir lernst du eine ganz andere Schneiderkunst, die ist anständig und ziemlich, zum Theil sehr ehrenvoll.“
sentences.l: “Ei, what,” answered the man, “you speak as you understand it: with me you learn quite another tailor’s art, it is decent and seemly, in part very honourable.”
sentences.i: “Oh, come,” answered the man, “you speak as much as you know of it: with me you will learn quite a different tailoring, one that is respectable and seemly, and in part very honourable.”
sentences.n: Ei was is a brush-aside, something like “oh, come now”. dus is du es run together — “as you understand it”, meaning: you judge by the little you know of it. ziemlich here keeps its old sense of “seemly, becoming”, from ziemen, to befit; the modern “fairly, rather” came later.

sentences.t: Da ließ er sich überreden, gieng mit und lernte die Kunst des Mannes aus dem Fundament.
sentences.l: Then he let himself be talked over, went along and learned the man’s art from the foundation.
sentences.i: So he let himself be persuaded, went along, and learned the man’s art from the ground up.
sentences.n: aus dem Fundament — “from the foundation”, thoroughly, from the ground up. gieng is the 1857 spelling of ging; mitgehen splits, leaving mit standing behind.

sentences.t: Beim Abschied gab ihm dieser eine Nadel und sprach „damit kannst du zusammen nähen was dir vorkommt, es sei so weich wie ein Ei oder so hart als Stahl;
sentences.l: At parting this one gave him a needle and said “with it you can sew together whatever comes before you, be it as soft as an egg or as hard as steel;
sentences.i: At parting the master gave him a needle and said, “with this you can sew together whatever comes your way, be it as soft as an egg or as hard as steel;
sentences.n: dieser, “this one”, points back to the master and not to the pupil. was dir vorkommt — whatever comes your way (vorkommen, separable). es sei is the subjunctive of concession, “be it”. Here Stahl is the noun, steel — not the past tense of stehlen, which the tale also uses later on. The speech runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: und es wird ganz zu einem Stück, daß keine Naht mehr zu sehen ist.“
sentences.l: and it becomes wholly into one piece, so that no seam more is to be seen.”
sentences.i: and it becomes all one piece, so that no seam can be seen any more.”
sentences.n: zu etwas werden — to turn into something. die Naht is the seam, from nähen, to sew. zu sehen sein is the standard German “is to be seen, can be seen”.

sentences.t: Als die bestimmten vier Jahre herum waren, kamen die vier Brüder zu gleicher Zeit an dem Kreuzwege zusammen, herzten und küßten sich und kehrten heim zu ihrem Vater.
sentences.l: When the appointed four years were around, the four brothers came together at the same time at the cross-way, hugged and kissed one another and turned home to their father.
sentences.i: When the appointed four years were up, the four brothers came together at the crossroads at the very same hour, embraced and kissed one another, and returned home to their father.
sentences.n: herum sein, of time, is “to be over, to be up”. Kreuzwege carries the old dative -e. sich herzen is to press to the heart, from das Herz; heim kehren is heimkehren, to return home, with the particle standing free.

sentences.t: „Nun,“ sprach dieser ganz vergnügt, „hat euch der Wind wieder zu mir geweht?“
sentences.l: “Well,” said this one quite delighted, “has the wind blown you back to me?”
sentences.i: “Well now,” said he, thoroughly pleased, “has the wind blown you back to me again?”
sentences.n: wehen — to blow, of the wind; geweht is its past participle. dieser again means “the latter”, here the father.

sentences.t: Sie erzählten wie es ihnen ergangen war und daß jeder das Seinige gelernt hätte.
sentences.l: They told how it had gone for them and that each had learned his own.
sentences.i: They told how they had fared and that each had learned his own trade.
sentences.n: es ist mir ergangen is an impersonal turn with the person in the dative: “it went for me”, that is, how I fared. das Seinige is “his own, his own share”. hätte is the subjunctive of reported speech, marking these as the brothers’ words and not the teller’s.

sentences.t: Nun saßen sie gerade vor dem Haus unter einem großen Baum, da sprach der Vater „jetzt will ich euch auf die Probe stellen und sehen was ihr könnt.“
sentences.l: Now they sat just in front of the house under a great tree, then the father said “now I will put you to the proof and see what you can do.”
sentences.i: Now they were sitting just outside the house under a great tree, and the father said, “now I will put you to the proof and see what you can do.”
sentences.n: auf die Probe stellen — to put to the proof. was ihr könnt has no main verb of doing: können alone carries “can do”.

sentences.t: Danach schaute er auf und sagte zu dem zweiten Sohne „oben im Gipfel dieses Baums sitzt zwischen zwei Ästen ein Buchfinkennest, sag mir wie viel Eier liegen darin?“
sentences.l: After that he looked up and said to the second son “up in the top of this tree there sits between two branches a chaffinch’s nest, tell me how many eggs lie in it?”
sentences.i: Then he looked up and said to the second son, “up in the crown of this tree there is a chaffinch’s nest between two branches; tell me how many eggs are lying in it.”
sentences.n: aufschauen — to look up (separable). Sohne keeps the old dative -e. Der Buchfink is the chaffinch, so a Buchfinkennest is a chaffinch’s nest; German says the nest sitzt in the tree where English would say it is there.

sentences.t: Der Sterngucker nahm sein Glas, schaute hinauf und sagte „fünfe sinds.“
sentences.l: The star-gazer took his glass, looked up and said “five they are.”
sentences.i: The star-gazer took his glass, looked up and said, “there are five.”
sentences.n: sein Glas is the spyglass of the unit before, not a drinking glass. fünfe is an older counting form of fünf, still heard in speech; sinds is sind es run together, “they are”.

sentences.t: Sprach der Vater zum ältesten „hol du die Eier herunter, ohne daß der Vogel, der darauf sitzt und brütet, gestört wird.“
sentences.l: Said the father to the eldest “fetch you the eggs down, without that the bird, which sits on them and broods, is disturbed.”
sentences.i: The father said to the eldest, “you fetch the eggs down without the bird that sits brooding on them being disturbed.”
sentences.n: The sentence opens with its verb, Sprach, and no introductory word — a lively narrative turn German allows and English cannot copy. hol du: the pronoun is added to the imperative to point at this son and no other. ohne daß introduces a clause where English says “without … being”. brüten is to brood, to sit on eggs.

sentences.t: Der kunstreiche Dieb stieg hinauf und nahm dem Vöglein, das gar nichts davon merkte und ruhig sitzen blieb, die fünf Eier unter dem Leib weg und brachte sie dem Vater herab.
sentences.l: The art-rich thief climbed up and took from the little bird, which noticed nothing at all of it and stayed sitting quietly, the five eggs away from under its body and brought them down to the father.
sentences.i: The skilful thief climbed up and took the five eggs from under the little bird’s body — it noticed nothing at all and sat quietly on — and brought them down to his father.
sentences.n: kunstreich, “rich in art”, is the word of the title: skilled, accomplished. dem Vöglein is the dative of the one robbed, where English needs “from the bird”. wegnehmen is split wide open here, nahm … weg, with the whole clause about the bird pushed in between.

sentences.t: Der Vater nahm sie, legte an jede Ecke des Tisches eins und das fünfte in die Mitte, und sprach zum Jäger „du schießest mir mit einem Schuß die fünf Eier in der Mitte entzwei.“
sentences.l: The father took them, laid one at each corner of the table and the fifth in the middle, and said to the huntsman “you shoot me the five eggs in two through the middle with one shot.”
sentences.i: The father took them, laid one at each corner of the table and the fifth in the middle, and said to the huntsman, “you shall shoot the five eggs in two through the middle with a single shot.”
sentences.n: schießest is the older long form of schießt, and the present tense here has the force of a command. mir is the ethic dative, an untranslatable “for me” that draws the speaker into the deed. entzwei — in two, apart.

sentences.t: Der Jäger legte seine Büchse an und schoß die Eier, wie es der Vater verlangt hatte, alle fünfe, und zwar in einem Schuß.
sentences.l: The huntsman laid his gun on and shot the eggs, as the father had demanded, all five, and that in one shot.
sentences.i: The huntsman levelled his gun and shot the eggs as the father had asked, all five, and that at a single shot.
sentences.n: anlegen, of a gun, is to bring it up and level it (separable: legte … an). und zwar picks up what was just said and pins it down: “and that indeed”.

sentences.t: Der hatte gewis von dem Pulver das um die Ecke schießt.
sentences.l: That one certainly had some of the powder that shoots around the corner.
sentences.i: He must certainly have had some of the powder that shoots round corners.
sentences.n: A dry aside from the teller; powder that shoots round corners is a stock piece of tall talk. Der at the head is the demonstrative “that one, he”, not the article. gewis is the 1857 spelling of gewiß.

sentences.t: „Nun kommt die Reihe an dich,“ sprach der Vater zu dem vierten Sohn, „du nähst die Eier wieder zusammen und auch die jungen Vöglein, die darin sind, und zwar so, daß ihnen der Schuß nichts schadet.“
sentences.l: “Now the row comes to you,” said the father to the fourth son, “you sew the eggs together again and also the young little birds that are inside them, and that in such a way that the shot does them no harm.”
sentences.i: “Now it is your turn,” said the father to the fourth son; “you shall sew the eggs together again, and the young birds inside them too, and so that the shot does them no harm.”
sentences.n: die Reihe kommt an dich — “the row comes to you”, the ordinary way of saying it is your turn. schaden takes the dative of the one harmed, ihnen.

sentences.t: Der Schneider holte seine Nadel und nähte wies der Vater verlangt hatte.
sentences.l: The tailor fetched his needle and sewed as it the father had demanded.
sentences.i: The tailor fetched his needle and sewed as his father had asked.
sentences.n: wies is wie es run together — “as it”, with an es that English leaves out.

sentences.t: Als er fertig war, mußte der Dieb die Eier wieder auf den Baum ins Nest tragen und dem Vogel, ohne daß er etwas merkte, wieder unter legen.
sentences.l: When he was finished, the thief had to carry the eggs again up the tree into the nest and lay them under the bird again, without its noticing anything.
sentences.i: When he had done, the thief had to carry the eggs back up into the nest in the tree and slip them under the bird again without its noticing.
sentences.n: unterlegen — to lay underneath; 1857 prints the particle separately, wieder unter legen. dem Vogel is again the dative of the one concerned.

sentences.t: Das Thierchen brütete sie vollends aus, und nach ein paar Tagen krochen die Jungen hervor und hatten da, wo sie vom Schneider zusammengenäht waren, ein rothes Streifchen um den Hals.
sentences.l: The little creature brooded them out to the end, and after a couple of days the young ones crept forth and had, there where they had been sewn together by the tailor, a little red stripe around the neck.
sentences.i: The little creature hatched them out, and after a few days the young ones crept forth with a small red stripe round the neck, just where the tailor had sewn them together.
sentences.n: ausbrüten — to hatch out (separable, split here by vollends, “right to the end”). Thierchen and Streifchen carry the diminutive -chen, which the tales use constantly for what is small; Thier is the 1857 spelling of Tier, rothes of rotes.

sentences.t: „Ja,“ sprach der Alte zu seinen Söhnen, „ich muß euch über den grünen Klee loben, ihr habt eure Zeit wohl benutzt und was rechtschaffenes gelernt: ich kann nicht sagen wem von euch der Vorzug gebührt.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said the old man to his sons, “I must praise you over the green clover, you have used your time well and learned something upright: I cannot say to whom of you the precedence is due.
sentences.i: “Well,” said the old man to his sons, “I must praise you to the skies: you have used your time well and learned an honest trade — I cannot say which of you deserves the first place.
sentences.n: über den grünen Klee loben, “to praise beyond the green clover”, is a set phrase for praising extravagantly, and is still said. was rechtschaffenes is etwas rechtschaffenes, “something proper”. gebühren, to be due, takes the dative wem. The speech runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: Wenn ihr nur bald Gelegenheit habt eure Kunst anzuwenden, da wird sichs ausweisen.“
sentences.l: If you only soon have occasion to apply your art, then it will show itself.”
sentences.i: If only you soon have occasion to use your craft, then it will show itself.”
sentences.n: anwenden — to apply, to put to use (separable). sichs is sich es run together; sich ausweisen is “to show itself, to become plain”.

sentences.t: Nicht lange danach kam großer Lärm ins Land, die Königstochter wäre von einem Drachen entführt worden.
sentences.l: Not long after that a great noise came into the land, the king’s daughter had been carried off by a dragon.
sentences.i: Not long after, a great outcry went through the land: the king’s daughter had been carried off by a dragon.
sentences.n: wäre … entführt worden is the subjunctive of reported speech — the news as people told it, not as the teller vouches for it. Lärm here is the noise of rumour, an outcry.

sentences.t: Der König war Tag und Nacht darüber in Sorgen und ließ bekannt machen wer sie zurück brächte, sollte sie zur Gemahlin haben.
sentences.l: The king was day and night in worries over it and had it made known, whoever brought her back should have her as wife.
sentences.i: Day and night the king was in distress over it, and had it proclaimed that whoever brought her back should have her to wife.
sentences.n: bekannt machen lassen — to have a thing made known, to proclaim it; lassen with an infinitive again. brächte is subjunctive, part of the proclamation as reported. die Gemahlin is the elevated word for a wife, a consort.

sentences.t: Die vier Brüder sprachen unter einander „das wäre eine Gelegenheit, wo wir uns könnten sehen lassen“ wollten zusammen ausziehen und die Königstochter befreien.
sentences.l: The four brothers said among one another “that would be an occasion where we could let ourselves be seen”, [and] wanted to set out together and free the king’s daughter.
sentences.i: The four brothers said among themselves, “that would be an occasion to show what we are worth,” and they made ready to set out together and free the king’s daughter.
sentences.n: sich sehen lassen — literally “to let oneself be seen”, that is, to show oneself to advantage. The sentence runs straight out of the quoted speech into wollten with no joining word and no repeated subject; the bracketed [and] in the literal line is supplied so that the English can stand — square brackets always mark words added here, never words in the 1857 text. ausziehen here is not “to pull out” but to set out, to march out.

sentences.t: „Wo sie ist, will ich bald wissen“ sprach der Sterngucker, schaute durch sein Fernrohr und sprach
sentences.l: “Where she is, I will soon know,” said the star-gazer, looked through his spyglass and said
sentences.i: “I shall soon know where she is,” said the star-gazer; he looked through his spyglass and said
sentences.n: The clause Wo sie ist stands first, which pushes the verb will into second place and leaves the subject ich after it — the V2 rule at work. The speech runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: „ich sehe sie schon, sie sitzt weit von hier auf einem Felsen im Meer und neben ihr der Drache, der sie bewacht.“
sentences.l: “I see her already, she sits far from here on a rock in the sea and beside her the dragon that guards her.”
sentences.i: “I see her already: she is sitting far from here on a rock in the sea, and beside her the dragon that keeps watch on her.”
sentences.n: und neben ihr der Drache has no verb of its own — the sitzt of the clause before carries over. der Felsen is a rock or crag.

sentences.t: Da gieng er zu dem König und bat um ein Schiff für sich und seine Brüder und fuhr mit ihnen über das Meer bis sie zu dem Felsen hin kamen.
sentences.l: Then he went to the king and asked for a ship for himself and his brothers and travelled with them over the sea until they came to the rock.
sentences.i: So he went to the king and begged a ship for himself and his brothers, and sailed with them over the sea until they came to the rock.
sentences.n: bitten um — to ask for. fahren covers travel by any vehicle or vessel, here by sea. In hin kamen the particle hin marks motion away from the speaker toward a goal.

sentences.t: Die Königstochter saß da, aber der Drache lag in ihrem Schooß und schlief.
sentences.l: The king’s daughter sat there, but the dragon lay in her lap and slept.
sentences.i: The king’s daughter sat there, but the dragon lay asleep in her lap.
sentences.n: Schooß is the 1857 spelling of Schoß, the lap. The picture is domestic and horrible at once, and the tale spends no word on it.

sentences.t: Der Jäger sprach „ich darf nicht schießen, ich würde die schöne Jungfrau zugleich tödten.“
sentences.l: The huntsman said “I may not shoot, I would kill the beautiful maiden at the same time.”
sentences.i: The huntsman said, “I dare not shoot: I would kill the fair maiden along with it.”
sentences.n: dürfen is leave or permission, not ability — “I am not at liberty to shoot”. tödten is the 1857 spelling of töten.

sentences.t: „So will ich mein Heil versuchen“ sagte der Dieb, schlich sich heran und stahl sie unter dem Drachen weg, aber so leis und behend, daß das Unthier nichts merkte, sondern fortschnarchte.
sentences.l: “Then I will try my luck,” said the thief, crept himself up and stole her away from under the dragon, but so softly and nimbly that the monster noticed nothing but snored on.
sentences.i: “Then I will try my fortune,” said the thief; he crept up and stole her out from under the dragon, but so softly and nimbly that the monster noticed nothing and snored on.
sentences.n: sein Heil versuchen — to try one’s luck; das Heil is fortune, deliverance, and not the adjective heil, “unhurt”. wegstehlen is split: stahl … weg. fortschnarchen is to snore on, with fort carrying “onward, without stopping”.

sentences.t: Sie eilten voll Freude mit ihr aufs Schiff und steuerten in die offene See:
sentences.l: They hurried full of joy with her onto the ship and steered into the open sea:
sentences.i: Full of joy they hurried aboard the ship with her and steered out into the open sea:
sentences.n: die See, feminine, is the sea as sailors name it; das Meer, used a few lines above, is the same water in the higher, more literary word. This is plain High German here, not a dialect form. The colon sets up the turn that follows.

sentences.t: aber der Drache, der bei seinem Erwachen die Königstochter nicht mehr gefunden hatte, hinter ihnen her und schnaubte wüthend durch die Luft.
sentences.l: but the dragon, which on its awakening had no longer found the king’s daughter, [came] after them and snorted furiously through the air.
sentences.i: but the dragon, which on waking had not found the king’s daughter any more, was after them, snorting furiously through the air.
sentences.n: The main verb is simply missing: after the long relative clause German can leave a verb of motion out and let the reader supply it. The bracketed [came] is added here so the English can stand — the 1857 text has no such word. hinter ihnen her marks pursuit; wüthend is the 1857 spelling of wütend.

sentences.t: Als er gerade über dem Schiff schwebte und sich herablassen wollte, legte der Jäger seine Büchse an und schoß ihm mitten ins Herz.
sentences.l: When it hovered just over the ship and wanted to let itself down, the huntsman laid his gun on and shot it right into the heart.
sentences.i: Just as it hovered over the ship and was about to drop down, the huntsman levelled his gun and shot it through the heart.
sentences.n: sich herablassen — to let oneself down, to descend. ihm is the dative of the creature struck: German shoots “to it into the heart” where English says “through its heart”.

sentences.t: Das Unthier fiel todt herab, war aber so groß und gewaltig, daß es im Herabfallen das ganze Schiff zertrümmerte.
sentences.l: The monster fell down dead, but was so big and mighty that in the falling-down it smashed the whole ship to pieces.
sentences.i: The monster fell down dead, but it was so huge and heavy that in falling it smashed the whole ship to pieces.
sentences.n: im Herabfallen — the infinitive turned into a noun with the article, “in the falling-down”, where English says “as it fell”. Unthier, 1857 for Untier, is a beast that is no proper beast: a monster.

sentences.t: Sie erhaschten glücklich noch ein paar Bretter und schwammen auf dem weiten Meer umher.
sentences.l: They snatched luckily still a couple of boards and swam about on the wide sea.
sentences.i: They managed to snatch a few planks and swam about on the wide sea.
sentences.n: glücklich in the older usage is “by good fortune, successfully”, not “happily”; it comes again at the end of this block. umherschwimmen is split: schwammen … umher.

sentences.t: Da war wieder große Noth, aber der Schneider, nicht faul, nahm seine wunderbare Nadel, nähte die Bretter mit ein paar großen Stichen in der Eile zusammen,
sentences.l: Then there was great distress again, but the tailor, not lazy, took his wondrous needle, sewed the boards together in haste with a couple of great stitches,
sentences.i: Now there was great distress again, but the tailor, losing no time, took his wondrous needle and sewed the planks together in haste with a few great stitches,
sentences.n: nicht faul is a fixed aside — “not slow about it”, without delay. die Noth, 1857 for Not, is need or distress, the tales’ word for any hard pass.

sentences.t: setzte sich darauf, und sammelte alle Stücke des Schiffs.
sentences.l: sat himself on it, and gathered all the pieces of the ship.
sentences.i: sat down on it and gathered all the pieces of the ship.
sentences.n: sich setzen is reflexive where English simply sits. des Schiffs is the genitive, “of the ship”.

sentences.t: Dann nähte er auch diese so geschickt zusammen, daß in kurzer Zeit das Schiff wieder segelfertig war und sie glücklich heim fahren konnten.
sentences.l: Then he sewed these too together so deftly that in a short time the ship was ready to sail again and they could travel home safely.
sentences.i: Then he sewed these together too, so deftly that in a short time the ship was fit to sail again and they could make their way safely home.
sentences.n: segelfertig — “sail-ready”, fit to put to sea; German builds such compounds freely. glücklich again means safely, by good fortune.

sentences.t: Als der König seine Tochter wieder erblickte, war große Freude.
sentences.l: When the king caught sight of his daughter again, there was great joy.
sentences.n: erblicken — to catch sight of, to spy, from der Blick, the glance. German leaves out the “there” that English needs before was.

sentences.t: Er sprach zu den vier Brüdern „einer von euch soll sie zur Gemahlin haben, aber welcher das ist, macht unter euch aus.“
sentences.l: He said to the four brothers “one of you shall have her as wife, but which that is, settle among yourselves.”
sentences.i: He said to the four brothers, “one of you shall have her to wife, but which one it is to be, settle that among yourselves.”
sentences.n: ausmachen — to settle, to agree (separable: macht … aus). welcher das ist stands in front as the thing to be settled, which German allows and English has to prop up with “that”.

sentences.t: Da entstand ein heftiger Streit unter ihnen, denn jeder machte Ansprüche.
sentences.l: Then a violent quarrel arose among them, for each made claims.
sentences.i: Then a fierce quarrel arose among them, for each put in his claim.
sentences.n: entstehen — to arise, to come about. Ansprüche machen, to make claims; der Anspruch is a claim, from ansprechen.

sentences.t: Der Sterngucker sprach „hätt ich nicht die Königstochter gesehen, so wären alle eure Künste umsonst gewesen: darum ist sie mein.“
sentences.l: The star-gazer said “had I not seen the king’s daughter, so would all your arts have been in vain: therefore she is mine.”
sentences.i: The star-gazer said, “if I had not seen the king’s daughter, all your arts would have been in vain: therefore she is mine.”
sentences.n: hätt ich nicht … is a conditional built without wenn: the verb comes first instead, and German answers it with so. The clipped hätt for hätte is the shape of speech. All four brothers argue in this same figure, three times more.

sentences.t: Der Dieb sprach „was hätte das Sehen geholfen, wenn ich sie nicht unter dem Drachen weggeholt hätte: darum ist sie mein.“
sentences.l: The thief said “what would the seeing have helped, if I had not fetched her away from under the dragon: therefore she is mine.”
sentences.i: The thief said, “what good would the seeing have been if I had not carried her off from under the dragon? Therefore she is mine.”
sentences.n: das Sehen — the infinitive as a noun again, “the seeing”. wegholen is split in the participle weggeholt: holen with the particle weg.

sentences.t: Der Jäger sprach „ihr wärt doch sammt der Königstochter von dem Unthier zerrissen worden, hätte es meine Kugel nicht getroffen: darum ist sie mein.“
sentences.l: The huntsman said “you would after all have been torn to pieces by the monster, together with the king’s daughter, had my ball not hit it: therefore she is mine.”
sentences.i: The huntsman said, “you would have been torn to pieces by the monster, and the king’s daughter with you, had my bullet not struck it: therefore she is mine.”
sentences.n: sammt, 1857 for samt, is “together with” and takes the dative. die Kugel is a ball — the bullet of a smooth-bore gun, not a ball or sphere in general. Again the conditional without wenn: hätte es … nicht getroffen.

sentences.t: Der Schneider sprach „und hätte ich euch mit meiner Kunst nicht das Schiff wieder zusammengeflickt, ihr wärt alle jämmerlich ertrunken: darum ist sie mein.“
sentences.l: The tailor said “and had I not patched the ship together again for you with my art, you would all have drowned miserably: therefore she is mine.”
sentences.i: The tailor said, “and if I had not patched the ship together again for you with my art, you would all have drowned miserably: therefore she is mine.”
sentences.n: zusammenflicken — to patch together; flicken is to mend a garment, the tailor’s own word for it. euch is the dative of the ones it was done for.

sentences.t: Da that der König den Ausspruch „jeder von euch hat ein gleiches Recht, und weil ein jeder die Jungfrau nicht haben kann, so soll sie keiner von euch haben,
sentences.l: Then the king made the pronouncement “each of you has an equal right, and because every one cannot have the maiden, so shall none of you have her,
sentences.i: Then the king gave his ruling: “each of you has an equal right, and since every one of you cannot have the maiden, none of you shall have her,
sentences.n: einen Ausspruch thun — to hand down a ruling; that is the 1857 spelling of tat. weil ein jeder die Jungfrau nicht haben kann puts the negation late, where English puts it early. The speech runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: aber ich will jedem zur Belohnung ein halbes Königreich geben.“
sentences.l: but I will give each one half a kingdom as reward.”
sentences.i: but I will give each of you half a kingdom as a reward.”
sentences.n: zur Belohnung — “as a reward”, with zu where English uses “as”.

sentences.t: Den Brüdern gefiel diese Entscheidung, und sie sprachen „es ist besser so, als daß wir uneins werden.“
sentences.l: To the brothers this decision was pleasing, and they said “it is better so, than that we become at odds.”
sentences.i: The brothers were pleased with this decision, and they said, “it is better so than that we should fall out.”
sentences.n: gefallen takes the dative of the person pleased, and the thing that pleases is the subject: “to the brothers the decision pleased”. uneins werden — to fall out, to be of one mind no longer, from un- and eins, “one”.

sentences.t: Da erhielt jeder ein halbes Königreich, und sie lebten mit ihrem Vater in aller Glückseligkeit, so lange es Gott gefiel.
sentences.l: Then each received half a kingdom, and they lived with their father in all bliss, so long as it pleased God.
sentences.i: So each received half a kingdom, and they lived with their father in all bliss as long as it pleased God.
sentences.n: so lange es Gott gefiel is the tales’ sober closing formula: happiness lasts as long as it is granted, and not for ever. gefallen again with the dative, here Gott.

glossary.ausziehen: ausziehen — to set out, to march out (separable: zog aus; elsewhere: to pull out)
glossary.diese: diese — this (fem. sg.); these, them (nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.ei: das Ei — egg; ei — well now, ah (interjection, Ei was)
glossary.eins: eins — one (neuter pronoun; legte … eins: laid one of them)
glossary.erwachen: erwachen — to awaken; das Erwachen — the waking (bei seinem Erwachen: on its waking)
glossary.fehlt: fehlen — misses (3rd sg.; of a gun, die fehlt nicht: that one never misses; ordinarily: to be lacking, to be wrong)
glossary.frage: die Frage — question (eine Frage an jemanden thun: to put a question to someone); frage — ask (imperative sg.)
glossary.fremde: die Fremde — foreign parts, the world away from home (in die Fremde gehen: to go out into the world)
glossary.fuhr: fahren — travelled, sailed (3rd sg. past; über das Meer fahren: to go by sea)
glossary.gefallen: gefallen — to please (sich etwas gefallen lassen: to put up with a thing, to be content with it); also the past participle of fallen, fallen
glossary.gilt: gelten — counts as, passes for (3rd sg.; für etwas gelten; also: to be worth)
glossary.glas: das Glas — glass; here the spyglass, the star-gazer’s telescope
glossary.heil: das Heil — luck, fortune, deliverance (sein Heil versuchen: to try one’s luck)
glossary.heran: heran — up, close, near (separable prefix; heranwachsen: to grow up; heran schleichen: to creep up)
glossary.junge: der Junge — boy, lad; also jung — young (inflected)
glossary.jungen: jung — young (adj., inflected); die Jungen — the young ones, the nestlings
glossary.korn: das Korn — the bead, the foresight of a gun (aufs Korn nehmen: to take aim at; elsewhere: grain)
glossary.kugel: die Kugel — ball; here the bullet of a gun
glossary.lehre: die Lehre — apprenticeship (in die Lehre nehmen: to take on as an apprentice)
glossary.müßt: müssen — must (2nd pl. present, ihr müßt; 1857 spelling of müsst)
glossary.naht: die Naht — seam (from nähen, to sew)
glossary.recht: das Recht — right, claim (ein gleiches Recht: an equal right); recht (adv.) — right, properly, quite
glossary.reihe: die Reihe — row; turn (die Reihe kommt an dich: it is your turn)
glossary.see: die See — the sea, the open sea (fem.; in die offene See steuern: to steer out into the open sea)
glossary.sei: sein — be it (3rd sg. subjunctive of concession, es sei so weich …); also sei — be (imperative sg.)
glossary.sicher: sicher — safe, secure; (adv.) surely, for certain (das triffst du sicher)
glossary.sonst: sonst — otherwise, else (sonst kein Mensch: no one else)
glossary.stahl: stehlen — stole (3rd sg. past); also der Stahl — steel (so hart als Stahl: as hard as steel)
glossary.stellen: stellen — to put, to place (auf die Probe stellen: to put to the proof; sich stellen: to place oneself)
glossary.vorhaben: das Vorhaben — intention, what one has in mind (from vorhaben, to intend; separable vor-)
glossary.weg: weg — away, off (adv. and separable prefix: wegnehmen, wegstehlen); der Weg — way, path (seinen Weg gehen: to go one’s way)
glossary.weiß: wissen — (I) know (1st sg. present, ich weiß); also weiß — white
glossary.welcher: welcher — which, which one (interrogative and relative; here masc. nom.)
glossary.werde: werden — become! (imperative sg., werde ein Dieb); also werden — to become, and the auxiliary will
glossary.zerrissen: zerreißen — torn to pieces (past participle; zerrissen worden: to have been torn apart)
glossary.zogen: ziehen — drew, went, marched (3rd pl. past; zum Thor hinaus ziehen: to march out through the gate; also: to pull)
